# Background & aims

1.  

# Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmmTMB)
library(easystats)
library(broom.mixed)
library(arrow)
library(modelbased)

data_traits_climate <-
  arrow::read_parquet("data-processed/data_traits_climate.parquet") |>
  select(decimal_longitude:life_stage, growth_form_simpler, life_history, woody) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log(annual_precipitation),
    log_value = log(value)
  ) |>
  # Let's also collect the mean rainfall and temp for each species, and devitations of each from their respective mean
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation_mn = mean(log_annual_precipitation),
    log_annual_precipitation_c = log_annual_precipitation - log_annual_precipitation_mn,
    average_temperature_mn = mean(average_temperature),
    average_temperature_c = average_temperature - average_temperature_mn
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # add a site index, based on unqiue lat, longley
  mutate(site_id = paste(decimal_longitude, decimal_latitude, sep= "-"))

data_traits_climate_woody <- data_traits_climate |>
  filter(woody == "woody")
```

# Comapring two methods: Straight Mixed effects models vs Cornwell-Ackerly Method

Let's try within species for LMA

```{r}
trait <- "leaf_mass_per_area"

data_model <- data_traits_climate_woody |>
  filter(trait_name == trait)

# model across species means
fit0 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c, data = data_model)
fit1 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c + (1 | taxon_name), data = data_model)
fit2 <- glmmTMB(log_value ~ log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c + (log_annual_precipitation_c | taxon_name), data = data_model)

# check support for random intercepts and slopes -- strong
anova(fit0, fit1, fit2)
```

Let's now extract fitted values and plot it. 

We want a plot with species means and global model added, so I'm going to extract several predicted values then join

```{r}
# overall fitted - with REs
data_fit2_re <- estimate_expectation(fit2) |>
  as_tibble()

# Global prediction - change in species mean trait with climate
data_fit2_global <- estimate_means(fit2, by = "log_annual_precipitation_mn") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  # change variable names so these will plot ok
  select(log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn, log_value = Mean) |>
  # backtransform so we can plot on raw scale
  mutate(
    annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation),
    value = exp(log_value),
    # need a taxon name for plotting
    taxon_name = "global average"
  )

# caluclate species means by removing devistations from center
data_fit2_mn <- estimate_expectation(fit2,
  data = data_fit2_re |> mutate(log_annual_precipitation_c = 0) |> select(-Predicted) |> distinct()
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  distinct()

# combine
data_fit2 <-
  data_fit2_re |>
  rename(log_value = Predicted) |>
  select(-SE, -Residuals) |>
  left_join(
    by = c("log_annual_precipitation_mn", "taxon_name"),
    data_fit2_mn |> select(log_annual_precipitation_mn, taxon_name, log_value_mn = Predicted)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    log_annual_precipitation = log_annual_precipitation_mn + log_annual_precipitation_c,
    annual_precipitation = exp(log_annual_precipitation),
    annual_precipitation_mn = exp(log_annual_precipitation_mn),
    value = exp(log_value),
    value_mn = exp(log_value_mn),
  )

# Choose a subset of taxa to plot. We'll choose randomly, but restrict to those with multiple sites and records
taxa <- data_model |>
  group_by(taxon_name) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_sites = n_distinct(annual_precipitation)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(n > 4, n_sites > 4) |>
  pull(taxon_name) |>
  unique() |>
  sample(30)

data_model_taxa <- data_model |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa) |>
  mutate(taxon2 = taxon_name)

data_fit2_taxa <- data_fit2 |>
  filter(taxon_name %in% taxa) |>
  mutate(taxon2 = taxon_name)

p_fit <-
  data_fit2 |>
  ggplot(aes(annual_precipitation, value, group = taxon_name)) +
  # raw data
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, col = "grey", data = data_model, stroke = 0) +
  # fitted lines
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5, col = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  # highlight certain species
  geom_point(aes(group = taxon2), col = "orange", show.legend = FALSE, data = data_model_taxa, size = 0.9, stroke = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(group = taxon2), col = "#d95f02", alpha = 1, show.legend = FALSE, data = data_fit2_taxa) +
  # global line
  geom_line(data = data_fit2_global, col = "red") +
  # species centers
  geom_point(aes(x = annual_precipitation_mn, y = value_mn, group = taxon2), col = "red", alpha = 1, size = 0.9,stroke = 0, data = data_fit2_taxa) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(y = trait, x = "annual rainfall") +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~taxon2)

ggsave("outputs/lma_species_panel.png", p_fit)
```

```{r}
# model across species means
parameters::parameters(fit2)
```

Plot random slopes. These are deviations from the average species response, which is negative. They should be centred around zero, which they are. 

```{r}
species_slopes_c <-
  broom.mixed::tidy(fit2, effects = "ran_vals") |>
  filter(term == "log_annual_precipitation_c") |>
  select(level, estimate) |>
  rename(taxon_name = level, slope_c = estimate)

# Range of within species slopes
stats::quantile(species_slopes_c$slope_c, probs = c(0.05, 0.5, 0.9))

ggplot(species_slopes_c, aes(slope_c)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

# Repeat for multiple traits

Let's now wrap into functions and repeat 

```{r}
source("R/fit_model_1D.R")

traits <- c(
  "leaf_mass_per_area", "leaf_area",
  "leaf_N_per_area", "leaf_P_per_area",
  "wood_density"
)

fits <- list()

climates <- c("log_annual_precipitation","average_temperature")

for (trait in traits) {
  for (climate in climates) {

  cat(trait, ":  ")
  data_model <- data_traits_climate |>
    filter(trait_name == trait)
  fits[[trait]] <- fit_model_1D(data_model, seed = 123, ind_variable= climate)
  ggsave(sprintf("outputs/%s_species_panel.png", paste0(trait,"_",climate)), fits[[trait]]$plot_fitted)
  }
}
```

Accessing fitted objects for more analysis

```{r}
names(fits)
names(fits[["leaf_mass_per_area"]])

parameters(fits[["leaf_mass_per_area"]][["fit"]])

parameters(fits[["wood_density"]][["fit"]])
```
